## DEC-148 — Wave 8, sync 1: the four plans approved; a baseline row is a composition, certificates carry a pinned design, and the ink guard is measured against the page

- **Date:** 2026-09-17 · **Decided by:** lead, on the four planning-first tasks (`docs/plan/notes/{branding,designer,console,platform}.md` at `574f556`, `85deba7`, `61cecd4`, `943f0d2`) and its own SCR-043 plan (`caf414c`)
- **Supersedes:** `REQ-DSG-026`'s roster count as `DEC-128` wrote it; `REQ-DSG-031`'s «serial range reserved»; `REQ-ADM-017`'s numeral clause (already withdrawn by `DEC-124`); `REQ-ADM-018`'s placement of scoring configuration changes; `09` SCR-043's mobile stepper; `16` §15 M12's and §16.5's migration numbers `0087`/`0088` (both now `checkin`'s — the studio's focal point needs no migration: `design_assets.focal_x/y` exist since `0055`).

### Contract 3 — what a baseline row is: a composition (`designer`'s option B)

`DEC-125` («the variant is the scheme, not a second template row»), `DEC-128`'s table (light and dark as
rows) and `REQ-DSG-026`'s acceptance («5 × 2 schemes and 3 × 2 orientations») disagreed. What actually
differs settles it. **A scheme is a palette**: every colour in a template is a `{{brand.*}}` token, so a
light row and a dark row would be byte-identical documents, and nothing in either could say which it is.
**An orientation is a composition**: measured on `attendance`, the portrait certificate `derive()`s from
the landscape master put every text layer in the top third of a 3508 px page, left a 1860 px empty band
and set the issue date at about 8 pt — and `safeAreaViolations()` reported nothing, because a safe-area
check cannot see a bad composition. Every portrait certificate issued so far ships that way.

**So:** 11 platform rows — the five poster families, and the three certificate families each landscape
and portrait (read from the master, no column) — each renderable in both schemes: 22 variants, counted
by literals in CI. One platform default per (purpose, family), the landscape row. `REQ-DSG-026`'s
acceptance is amended to this. `DEC-128`'s «both schemes, chosen at issue time» is honoured by the next
section, not by rows.

### Certificates carry a pinned design — `ENT-session_certificate_designs` and `certificates.scheme`

Automatic issuance has no human at issue time — it is the edge into `completed` — so a choice made «at
issue time» must be stored before it. **`ENT-session_certificate_designs`** is added, an amendment to the
frozen `02` §4.12 made under this entry: `org_id`, `session_id`, `kind` (`attendance` | `presenter`),
`template_id` (a certificate template of the kind's family, org or platform), `scheme` (a new
`brand_scheme` enum), `updated_by`, `updated_at`; `unique (session_id, kind)`; RLS enabled, staff read,
no write grant — written only through `set_certificate_design()` (`assert_fresh_admin()`, audited), which
refuses once a certificate of that kind for that session is issued or revoked. No row is today's
behaviour: the family default, `light`. **`certificates.scheme brand_scheme not null default 'light'`**
pins the scheme beside `template_version_id`, because a reissue years later must know it and nothing
else records it (`REQ-CRT-014`); the default is true of every existing row. `issue_certificate()` is
re-created **from `0088`'s text**, so `DEC-141`'s removed-check-in filter survives. Invariant 5 in full.

### Four findings that change the work, each accepted

1. ★ **A dark poster voids the blank-capture guard.** `inkedRatio()` and the harness's `inkOf()` count a
   pixel as ink when any channel is below 240; on a `#111a2c → #1d2a42` background every pixel is ink,
   so a poster whose text never painted (`DEC-024`'s blank goldens) would read 100 % inked and ship.
   **Ink is now measured against the page's own background** (a second capture with the layers hidden),
   landed before any call site passes `'dark'`.
2. ★ **`validate.ts` refused a gradient**, and both worker tasks call it: a gradient template promoted
   before the fix would make every automatic poster throw. **The promotion order is a hard dependency:**
   `branding`'s types (`391150e`) → the guard and `validate.ts` → `branding`'s renderer paints the
   gradient → `designer`'s seed. Promoted before the renderer, every regenerated poster renders silently
   on the `#ffffff` fallback.
3. ★ **`0055`'s no-hex guard does not walk gradient stops** (nor `rgb()`, `hsl()` or named colours on
   any field). `designer`'s first proposed file re-creates it as an **allowlist of the
   `{{brand.<identifier>}}` shape** over every colour-bearing value; token membership stays in TypeScript.
4. ★ **`getBrandKit()` would have taken down every `/app` page.** `canvasRaise` became a required key
   when the runtime's `dist` was rebuilt, while `brand_kit()` returned nine keys; the app layout reads the
   kit for every member. `6b3ac7f` fills a missing token from the platform default before parsing —
   which is also what keeps a merge-before-push deploy safe.

### The rest of the rulings

- **`designer`:** the M12 subset in — the editor's top bar, tabbed rail and inspector (`DEC-093`'s
  demotion), checks that select their layer, the variant strip from ready artifacts, align on the
  **document's** axis (`DEC-096`), layer order; **out** — drag, resize, rotate, snapping, marquee,
  distribute, nudge, focal point. The `PosterPicker` three-card chooser with a detach confirm naming the
  session is in (props unchanged). The certificate **mode stays on SCR-043**; SCR-045 carries the design,
  eligibility and the release. «من حضر وقيّم» (eligibility by having rated) is refused — a certificate's
  existence would disclose who rated (`REQ-RAT-004`). Phone «approve» is «اطلب التصدير». **No existing
  parity golden moves**; a separate background block adds `gradient-rtl`/`gradient-ltr` goldens and
  asserts the LTR capture equals the flipped RTL one. **The v2 posters bind the Knowledge Network rule to
  `{{brand.edgeStrong}}`**: `spine` is 1.05:1 on `canvasRaise`, so the motif vanished at the gradient's lit
  end (decorative, no WCAG failure; the owner may reverse it). A poster's scheme is not choosable this
  wave. A re-added member's missing certificate is not this wave (`unique (org_id, session_id,
  member_id, kind)` would need a product ruling on a new serial); SCR-045 shows the state instead.
- **`branding`:** the `'light'` default leaves all three signatures (every caller already passes one);
  `backgroundCss()` is exported so the harness and the swatch use the renderer's own string; the mirror
  lives in `render.ts` alone; contrast is displayed, not enforced, this wave (enforcement is M13's).
- **`console`:** badge **creation** is in (`REQ-REC-001` asks for it); the app never imports
  `worker/src/**`; the email templates' required fields stay admin-editable this wave — **a live
  `REQ-NTF-007` weakness carried for `notify`/M12**; the scoring screen's typed session UUID becomes a

- **`platform`:** break-glass **refreshes the token in the submit path** on start and on stop, proven on

- **The lead's SCR-043:** one scroll in four groups on a phone rather than `09`'s stepper; relational

A scoped one-off `regenerate_poster` enqueue for **live** posters of sessions with `starts_at > now()`,

## DEC-149 — Wave 8, sync 2: what a form control shows survives React's reset; break-glass says it opens nothing; the library seed is a migration now

- **Date:** 2026-09-17 · **Decided by:** lead, from the builds at `a4d2886`, `381a05f`, `fa93a98`, `5a8f5bc` and `bb3e290` and the captures opened on each

### 1 · Every `<form action>` submission resets the form, and the primitives carry the repair

React calls the native `form.reset()` at the end of the commit's mutation phase after **every** `<form
action>` submission, a refusal and a success alike (verified in the vendored `react-dom`:
`startHostTransition` → `requestFormReset` → `recursivelyResetForms`). A reset returns each control to its
default. React keeps an input's and a textarea's default in step with its props, but **not a select's**
(`defaultValue` marks an option at mount only; a controlled `value` marks none) **and not a controlled
checkbox's or radio's**. So a refused form showed the value a control mounted with while its state held
another, and the next submission posted what was on show. `console` found it on the manual award; the
lead's schedule form had six such controls, so a second «احفظ التعديلات» after a publish would have put
the page's first values back.

- **Decision.** The repair lives in `ui/select`, `ui/switch`, `ui/radio-group` and `ui/checkbox` (the
  lead, as custodian of `sessions`' primitives, `dcd5f05`): a controlled control is put back to its value in
  a layout effect, which runs after the reset in the same commit; an uncontrolled select makes the
  member's own change its default. A form that must come back empty after a success remounts with a `key`.
  No wrapper per call site — `console`'s `KeptSelect` was deleted (`b12a7b6`).
- `tests/components/ui/form-reset.test.tsx` pins the defect on the raw elements beside each repair.

### 2 · Break-glass opens no org screen, and every sentence now says so

Under `DEC-055` option C an impersonation session carries no member id, so every org route lands on
`/no-access`. The console's home, SCR-085, the banner and the lead's `/no-access` body all said or implied
that a session opens the org. **Decision:** the copy says what is true — time-limited, recorded in the
org's own audit log, the org's screens do not open (`1f1ced9`, `d82c7a1`). **Option A — a browsable,
read-only `impersonating` state in `session.ts` — is the owner's to schedule**; it is not wave 8's.

### 3 · `0098` is the library seed, and a migration is forward-only

`designer`'s generated seed became `0098_certificate_library.sql`. **Decision:** a later change to
`library.ts` ships as a **new** seed migration; `0098` is never regenerated. The drift test reads the latest
version of each composition across every seed, so a new seed passes it and an edited `0098` would too —
the rule is a review rule, recorded here so nobody "regenerates the seed".

### 4 · Smaller rulings

- **`DEC-145`'s orphaned streaming segment is not fixed this wave.** `wave8-designer-*` specs found a second
  hidden copy of a page's content under `div[hidden][id^="S:"]`; the rule stands — **locators under `/app`
  scope to `#main`** — and the defect stays M13's.
- **Viewport captures run with `reducedMotion: "reduce"`.** `globals.css` smooth-scrolls under
  `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`, so a capture taken right after a scroll showed the top of the
  page.
- **Lazily mounted card media must be scrolled into view and marked rendered before a capture**, or a blank
  render cannot be told from an unmounted one — the ink guard's whole point.
- **`controlClass`'s `w-full` beats a caller's `w-*`** (Tailwind emits `.w-full` after the fixed widths), so
  every `<Input className="w-32">` is full width. **Carried to M13**: dropping `w-full` when an unprefixed
  width is passed would narrow fields on screens whose captures are closed.
- **An org admin never reads a plan identifier.** The audit log's raw action key and the email studio's
  `MSG-*` ids are dropped from cards; rows still link by key.
- **Recognition edits write no audit or history row** — recorded, not built this wave.
- **Documents changed:** `STATUS.md`, `03-permissions-rls.md` §8.2 (`0099`'s ten rows, by the promotion)

## DEC-150 — Wave 9 is multi-day sessions, built on a day entity the lead lands first; the tracks meet in the data, so the wave is measured by its seams; `notify` runs, and `checkin` and `scoring` become opus

- **Date:** 2026-09-17 · **Decided by:** owner (the wave-9 brief, `docs/plan/notes/wave-9-lead.md`: the five tracks, the four rulings, the two added definitions of done), the file-level map, the contracts and the foundation's mechanism by the lead
- **Supersedes:** `DEC-147`'s wave-8 map as the map in force (kept in `CLAUDE.md` as the record); `DEC-147`'s transfer of `admin/sessions/[id]/schedule/**` and `messages/*/schedule.json` to the lead (they go to `sessions`, which builds `REQ-SES-016` in them); `DEC-137`'s placement of `app/me/{points,calendar,notifications}/**`, `components/scoring/{points-history-list,points-catalogue}.tsx`, `components/notifications/{notification-list,preference-matrix}.tsx` and their DAL modules with `content` (they return to `scoring` and `notify`, which are spawned); `DEC-147`'s placement of `messages/*/{scoring,notifications}.json` with `console` (not spawned); `REQ-SES-015`'s and `02` `ENT-session_days`' sentence «a task for the whole workshop is a task on day 1» (already superseded in substance by `DEC-121`; the PRD line is corrected with this entry).

### Why this wave is measured differently

Waves 6–8 moved routes onto a system and counted routes. This wave adds an entity under seven existing
tables on a live database, and **no route count can say whether it worked**. The measure is two
demonstrables (`STATUS.md`, wave-9 block): a three-day workshop end to end, and **a one-day session
behaving exactly as it does on `main`, proven by the existing suites passing with their assertions
untouched**. `STATUS.md` therefore carries a **contract list** — the seams between tracks — instead of a
route checklist, and an **untouched-suite ledger**: every pre-existing test file a wave-9 commit modifies
is named there with the reason, and an unexplained edit to an existing assertion is a defect.

### The foundation — the lead's, landed before any teammate's SQL (`0100`)

**One rule decides every choice below: `main`'s app and `main`'s worker must be correct on the new schema**,
because the owner pushes migrations before merging (the order waves 7 and 8 used) and both deploy from
`main`. So the wave is **additive**: no column is dropped or renamed, and no function `main` calls loses the
name and named arguments `main` sends. A contracting migration — dropping what the new code no longer
reads — is a later wave's, never this one's.

1. **`ENT-session_days`** as `02` defines it (`org_id`, `session_id`, `position`, `starts_at`, `ends_at`,
   `venue_id` or the custom-venue trio), RLS on, one `select` policy that defers to `sessions`' own
   visibility, `grant select` to `authenticated`, no write policy (every write is a definer RPC, as for
   every scheduling column since `0010`), a generated-sweep row and fixture rows. **`position` is derived
   and stored** — the chronological rank, renumbered by trigger — because days of one session cannot
   overlap, so their order is total and a hand-written position can only disagree with it.
2. ★ **`sessions.starts_at`, `ends_at`, `venue_id` and the custom-venue trio are derived and stored.**
   The window is the first day's start and the last day's end; **the venue is the first day's** — `DEC-119`
   names only the window, but the venue columns cannot be dropped (additive) and `0010`'s publish check
   reads them, so they need one meaning, and «where it begins» is the one a card can show.
   **Two triggers keep the pair in step, and a third checks it at commit:**
   - `session_days` → `sessions` (any `n`): after any day write, renumber, then update the session **only
     where a value is distinct** — so `sessions_notify`, the poster hook and the reminder schedule fire
     exactly when they fire today.
   - `sessions` → `session_days` (**`n ≤ 1` only**): a writer that still writes the session's own window —
     `main`'s `schedule_session()`, and every fixture and spec that inserts or moves a session directly,
     of which there are more than forty — gets its one day created, moved or removed with it. **This is
     what makes «a one-day session is a session with one day» true of rows nobody migrated by hand**, and
     it is a shim for writers, never a reader's branch.
   - a **deferred constraint trigger**: at commit, a session with days stores exactly its derived window
     and venue, and a session at `published` or beyond has at least one day. A day-aware writer sets the
     transaction-local `kareem.days_writer` and the second trigger stands down for it; the commit check
     never does.
3. **The backfill is the second trigger's own rule applied to every row**: each session with both ends
   gets one day carrying its window and venue; a session with neither gets none. `check_in_codes`,
   `check_ins` and `check_in_attempts` gain `session_day_id`, backfilled to that day; **`check_ins` and
   `check_in_codes` `not null` afterwards**, filled for legacy inserters by their `before insert` trigger
   (the code's day; else the day whose window, to `ends_at + 2 h`, contains `now()`, the later-started if
   two do; else the latest day already begun). `check_ins.session_window` becomes **the day's** window.
   `check_ins_session_member_active_uq` moves to `(session_day_id, member_id)`, and the exclusion
   constraint is re-created **after** it, as `0087` did, so a duplicate is still refused `23505` and not
   `23P01` (wave 8's rehearsal met exactly that inversion). `materials`, `session_tasks` and `photos` gain a
   **nullable** `session_day_id` with **no backfill** — null is the whole session (`DEC-121`) — a composite
   foreign key `(session_id, session_day_id)` so a day-scoped item can only name a day of its own session,
   and **`on delete set null (session_day_id)`**, which *is* `DEC-121`'s «deleting a day promotes its
   content to the session». `sessions.require_all_days boolean not null default true` sits beside
   `certificate_mode` (`REQ-SES-017`).
4. **Tables are the lead's; behaviour is the tracks'.** Every `alter table` of the wave goes through the
   lead (`0100` and, after sync 1, `calendar_events`); a teammate proposes functions, policies and triggers
   under `supabase/proposed/<name>/`. **A function has one writer**: where two tracks meet in one function,
   the owner of the function calls a function the other track owns (contract 5).

### The contracts — published before anyone spawns, in full in `STATUS.md`

1. **lead → all: the day set is the truth and the session window is its stored shadow.** Nobody computes a
   minimum or a maximum in TypeScript; a reader that needs the session's window reads `sessions`, a reader
   that needs days reads `session_days` by `position`.
2. **lead → all: additive, and `main` is correct on it.** `sessions.check_in_open` keeps its meaning at
   `n = 1`; reminder job keys and the ICS `UID` of a one-day session do not change, so a job or a calendar
   entry that exists today is moved, never duplicated.
3. **`sessions` → all: `schedule_session()`'s day set and `listSessionDays()`.** Two trailing parameters,
   `p_days jsonb default null` and `p_require_all_days boolean default null`; null is today's call. Days are
   matched by `id`; a day left out is deleted, refused if it holds attendance. `SessionDay` and a
   `cache()`-wrapped `listSessionDays()` are published from `lib/dal/sessions.ts` on day one and every track
   reads days through them.
4. **`checkin` → `sessions`, `scoring`, `content`: the day's check-in.** Every check-in RPC keeps
   `p_session` and gains a trailing `p_day uuid default null`; null resolves the day exactly as `0100`'s
   trigger does. The switch and the `ends_at + 2 h` ceiling are the day's.
5. **`checkin` ⇄ `scoring`: one call when attendance changes.** `check_in()`, `mark_checked_in_manually()`
   and `remove_check_in()` stop deciding what to award and call `scoring`'s `attendance_recorded()` and
   `attendance_removed()`; `scoring` publishes them first with `main`'s behaviour, then `checkin` switches.
6. **`scoring` → lead (as `designer`'s custodian), `content`: the attendance predicate.**
   `session_attendance_complete(p_session, p_member)` is the only definition of «attended the session» for
   points and certificates; `has_checked_in()` — any day, unchanged — stays the definition for rating,
   photos and a session-scoped «بعد» material. The award's key is per member per session **and must
   survive wave 7's remove → re-add**, which a naive per-session key turns into a net zero.
7. **`content` → `sessions`: the three slots group themselves.** `SlotProps` does not change; a slot reads
   days through contract 3, renders flat at `n ≤ 1`, and renders group headings as `<h3>` — the page still
   owns the `<h2>`. `sessions` publishes the one day-label formatter.
8. **`notify` ← 1, 3: one calendar entry and one reminder stream per day**, with contract 2's identities
   held at `n = 1`.
9. **lead → all: `src/lib/session-status.ts`.** `PhaseInput` gains `days`; `live` is «a day is running»,
   `ended` is «the last day has ended», and between two days a session is `open` — never a seventh phase;
   `dayPhase()` and `checkInDay()` are exported for the matrix and the slots. At `n ≤ 1` every function
   returns what it returns today, asserted by the existing unit suite unmodified.
10. **lead: `REQ-TSK-002` is enforced, not remembered.** A test fails if any check-in function's source, or
    any module in the check-in import graph, names `session_tasks`, `task_completions` or
    `task_form_responses`.

### Staffing — one addition to the brief, and two models raised

- ★ **`notify` runs as a fifth teammate.** The brief names `checkin`, `sessions`, `content` and `scoring`.
  `DEC-119` moves `calendar_events` to the day and makes reminders fire per day, and `REQ-SES-015`'s

  `content` stays sonnet; `sessions` and `notify` are opus already.
- **Not spawned, held by the lead as custodian:** `event`, `designer`, `console`, `platform`, `branding`.

## DEC-151 — Wave 9, sync 1: five plans approved; a day's ceiling is capped by the next day's start; the award is guarded by a standing-award check, not by its key alone; day changes are announced by a call, not a trigger; and four defects are caught on paper

- **Date:** 2026-09-17 · **Decided by:** lead (wave 9, sync 1), from the five plans in `docs/plan/notes/{sessions,checkin,content,scoring,notify}.md` «Wave 9 plan», each read in full
- **The foundation held.** `0100` alone: the **entire existing RLS suite passed unmodified** (833 cases) plus the generated sweep's new `session_days` row; `0101` the same. `tests/unit/{session-status,session-matrix}.test.ts` unmodified and green on contract 9. **One existing test file changed** (`admin-audit-labels.test.ts`, through its own exemption list — a custom Postgres setting must contain a dot); the ledger has the line.

### Four defects found by reading, before any code existed

1. **`checkin` — reopening one day would have opened every day.** Its plan kept `sessions.check_in_open` as a shadow (`bool_or` of the days) with two triggers: days → session, and session → **every** day, for legacy writers. Reopening day 2 of three closed days flips the shadow false → true, and the second trigger then carries «open» onto days 1 and 3. **Ruling:** the session → days direction acts only for a writer of the **session's** column; the shadow's own recompute marks itself (a transaction-local setting, **reset after its update**, as `kareem.days_writer` is never left on) and the second trigger stands down for it. A `pg_trigger_depth()` test is refused: it would also silence a legitimate session-level write made from inside any other trigger.
2. **`scoring` — a second award while the first still stands.** Its key is `check_in:check_in:<the member's latest active check-in>:<member>:v1` — at one day literally `main`'s key, and it survives remove → re-add, which a literal per-session key does not. But the key alone is not idempotent **per session**: with `require_all_days = false`, or a late manual mark after the award, a **new** active check-in advances the epoch to a new key while the first award stands — a silent double-pay on an append-only ledger. **Ruling:** the one per-member routine decides under a per-`(session, member)` advisory lock, from two facts — *is attendance complete* (contract 6) and *is there a standing attendance award for this session and member* (an award row no `reversal` points at): complete and none standing → award; not complete and one standing → reverse; otherwise nothing. The key stays as designed and becomes the **second** line of defence. The same check sits in `award_points()` for `source = 'check_in'`, because the job runs after the decision. **Inert at one day:** a second active check-in on the one day cannot exist.
3. **`content` — a presenter of a ONE-day session would have seen group headings.** Its grouping kept empty buckets for a manager (so each has an «أضف»), and at one day that is two buckets — «للورشة كاملة» and «اليوم الأول» — on a session that `REQ-SES-018` says has no scope concept at all. And a session cut back from two days to one may hold content still scoped to the remaining day, which a session-bucket-only flat list would **hide**. **Ruling:** with at most one day the three slots render **every** item flat, whatever its `session_day_id`; day groups exist only when there is more than one day to tell apart. That test is the specification's own (`REQ-SES-018`, first acceptance bullet) and says so in a comment.
4. **`content` — `create or replace` with a tenth parameter creates a second overload.** `record_photo_upload()` gains `p_uploaded_at`; `main`'s worker calls it with nine positional arguments, which would become ambiguous beside a ten-parameter twin. The nine-parameter signature is **dropped in the same file** (`0085`'s lesson, rule 2).

### The rulings

- **A day's check-in ceiling is capped by the next day's start** — `least(ends_at + 2 h, next.starts_at)` (`checkin`'s recommendation). Uncapped, a 9–12 and a 13–16 day on one date both hold 13:30: the clock names day 2 while an explicit day still reaches day 1, and a day-1 check-in records a person at a meeting that ended ninety minutes ago. Capped, the windows of one session's days never overlap. The cost — a morning room loses its grace once the afternoon begins — is released by the admin's uncapped manual mark (`REQ-CHK-017`). **It is one function, the lead's** (`check_in_ceiling()`, `0101`), because `resolve_session_day()` must use the same cap; its twin is `checkInCeiling()` in `session-status.ts`. Inert at one day by arithmetic.
- **`resolve_session_day()` has a third rule the contract's shorthand omitted**: nothing having begun, **the first day** — `fixture-m2` checks a member in to a session a day ahead, and `main` allows it. The gates still answer `not_started`; the resolver only has to land somewhere.
- **The attempt rate limit is per day**, as `REQ-SES-015` says («its own rate-limit stream»), not per session as `checkin` proposed. The two differ only when two days fall within ten minutes, where the requirement is explicit.
- ★ **Contract 5 gains a third hook, and contract 11 is new.**
  - **Certificates follow attendance through one function of the lead's** (as `designer`'s custodian, row L4): `attendance_certificate_sync(p_session, p_member)` — revoke when contract 6's predicate is false; **enqueue the issue job when it is true, the session is completed and no live certificate exists**. `checkin`'s three functions call it beside `scoring`'s two; `scoring`'s `attendance_removed()` is **points only**, as it planned, and `remove_check_in()` stops choosing a certificate by `check_in_id`, because removing day 1 must revoke a certificate that names day 3. The second half closes wave 7's carry — a member re-added after a removal gets no new certificate — which multi-day makes ordinary: an admin corrects the last day's list the next morning.
  - **Contract 11 — `sessions` → `notify`: `session_days_changed(p_session, p_before jsonb, p_after jsonb)`**, called once at the end of a day-aware `schedule_session()`. Both plans proposed a trigger on `session_days`; a row trigger fires mid-write, so a guard that de-duplicates a multi-row change sends the **first** row's partial truth and suppresses the rest — move days 2 and 3 and the member is told about day 2. The one day-aware writer already holds the whole before and after. It announces what `sessions_notify` cannot see (a day ≥ 2 moved, a day added or removed, the last end), reschedules reminders and enqueues the calendar jobs; at one day the legacy path never calls it, so **one notice, byte-identical, by construction**.
- **Reminders per day: an offset fires for day `k` only when its moment falls after day `k − 1` has ended** (`notify`'s rule). No threshold, no list of «long» offsets: three consecutive evenings get the 2-hour reminder each day and the 1-day and 7-day once; three monthly meetings get all three each time; at one day there is no previous day and the three jobs under the three keys are today's. Identity suffixes are by **position**, position 1 carrying today's key and `UID`. A day added or removed reuses `MSG-session_changed` with a `days` entry — no new `MSG-*` key.
- **Tables are the lead's, with one carried line.** `calendar_events`' old `unique (member_id, session_id)` is named by `main`'s `record_calendar_sync()` in `on conflict`, so it must leave **in the same file** as the function that replaces it, or every calendar sync fails `42P10` in between. `0101` adds the new rule beside it; the `drop constraint` is one lead-authored line carried verbatim at the top of `notify`'s proposed file. `0101` also gives a legacy insert its day — left null, `main`'s rows would read as «the day is gone» and the new worker would delete an entry the member was just given.
- **Reading days.** `listSessionDays(locale, sessionId)` — two arguments, the house DAL shape and the right `cache()` key. A **list over many sessions** may embed `session_days(…)` in its own query (the timeline, `listSyncedEvents()`); a single session goes through `listSessionDays()`. `SessionDay` carries `checkInOpen`; `DayWindow.checkInOpen` is optional. `sessions` counts a day's content in its own schedule query; `content` publishes no count.
- **Smaller rulings.** `sessions.duration_minutes` is day one's length. `schedule_session()` with a null `p_days` on a session that has several days is refused **by name** (`days_required`), not left to the commit check. Any `check_ins` row, removed or not, holds its day — the foreign key already says so. `p_days` is capped at 30. A multi-day award waits for completion even when `require_all_days` is false — one timing axis. A day added after a one-day award was paid is reversed at completion with its own reason, the certificate and the points agreeing. The completion evaluation folds into `evaluate_no_shows` (key unchanged, `0081`'s precedent). A partial attendee is not a no-show. A day-scoped «بعد» material releases when its day has ended **or its session has**. A material's re-scope is audited, for the reason `0052` audits its phase: it moves a visibility boundary. The photo fallback is the day whose nearer edge is closest. `tests/components/checkin/schedule-form.test.tsx` and `tests/e2e/checkin-schedule-walk-ins.spec.ts` follow the screen to `sessions`.
- ★ **Named differences at one day — each a fix, each approved here, each with its own new test, none asserted by an existing one.** «Byte-identical» means no regression, not the preservation of a defect: (1) `rotate_codes` stops minting codes for a session left `in_progress` past its ceiling — unusable codes, `REQ-CHK-016`; (2) `evaluate_company_points()` rule 2 excludes removed check-ins — the one reader `0088`'s sweep missed; (3) a member re-added after completion gets their certificate — wave 7's carry; (4) `{{startsAt}}` in mail is formatted rather than printed as a raw ISO instant — **conditional on `notify` showing the raw string in a real Mailpit capture first**.
- **Carried out of the wave, stated:** recognition edits' audit rows (wave 10, with `console`); `sessions_notify()` not announcing an end-time-only change at one day (unchanged, contract 2); the filter sheet's date mask and `ratings.edited_at` (wave 10, with the survey).
- **Supersedes:** `DEC-150` contract 4's «whether a day's ceiling is capped … is ruled at sync 1» (ruled: capped) and its two-rule shorthand for the resolver; `DEC-150` contract 5's two hooks (three); `DEC-150`'s map for the two schedule-form tests.
- **Documents changed:** `STATUS.md` (contracts 4, 5, 11; the named differences; sync 1), `03-permissions-rls.md` §5.2 and §8.2 (`0100`'s eleven rows, `0101`'s five), `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/agents/{sessions,checkin,scoring,notify,content}.md` (the rulings that move a file or a function), a migration (`0101`)

## DEC-152 — A live security hole, found by `checkin` and closed in its own migration: the private function that mints a check-in code was executable by `anon` since M2

- **Date:** 2026-09-17 · **Decided by:** lead, on `checkin`'s finding (commit `ec9b121`), verified before it was believed
- **The hole.** `public._issue_check_in_code(uuid)` (`0015`, M2) is `SECURITY DEFINER`, reads the session with RLS bypassed, **checks no caller**, and returns — or mints — the **live** check-in code. `0015` created it and never revoked it, and a new function is `execute`-to-`PUBLIC` by default, so PostgREST served it to **`anon`**. **Proven, not inferred**: against local Supabase, `POST /rest/v1/rpc/_issue_check_in_code` with the publishable key alone and a session id returned `{ "code": "QH…", "valid_until": … }`, while the guarded sibling `ensure_check_in_code()` — «presenter of the session, or staff», the only door a screen uses — answered `42501` to the same call. **A session's id is not a secret**: it is in the public share link `/s/<id>` (`REQ-SES-013`). It is live on production today.
- **What it allowed.** (1) A member of the org reads the rotating code **without being in the room** and checks in from anywhere — attendance points and a certificate for a session they did not attend, which is the one thing a code read aloud exists to prevent (`REQ-CHK-001`, `REQ-CHK-009`, D24). (2) Anyone at all writes `check_in_codes` rows into any org's session. **What it did not allow:** checking in without being an active member of that org holding a seat (or with walk-ins on) — `check_in()` still decides that. There is no evidence either way that it was used: a call leaves only a `check_in_codes` row, indistinguishable from a rotation.
- **Decision.** (1) **`0103` is the revoke `0015` forgot, in its own file**, ahead of `checkin`'s per-day rewrite: `revoke execute … from public, anon, authenticated, service_role`. Its three callers are all definer and run as the owner, so nothing needs the grant. ★ **It is idempotent, so the owner may run the one statement against production today**, before the wave is rehearsed or pushed, and the migration then changes nothing — `STATUS.md` has it verbatim. A privilege change is schema, not data, so `DEC-023`'s «never a data fix as a migration» is not engaged; running it early by hand is the owner's call, not a session's. (2) **The mirror image of invariant 6 is now a test.** «Every policy has a matching grant» has a twin nobody had written down — **every definer function has a deliberate grant** — and `tests/rls/definer-exposure.test.ts` is that sentence, generated over the catalogue: the `SECURITY DEFINER`, non-trigger functions `anon` may execute are **exactly** a documented six (`session_public_card`, `verify_certificate`, `export_is_public_card`, and three that answer only about the caller), and no function whose name begins with an underscore is executable by any client role. A new function fails the suite until it is revoked or listed with its reason. It would have failed at M2.
- **Swept, not assumed.** Every other definer function open to `anon` is a trigger function — which Postgres refuses to call directly whatever its ACL — or one of the six. One low finding recorded and not fixed here: `session_venue_label(uuid, text)` (`0036`, `notify`'s) is open to `authenticated` with no caller check, so a member who already holds another org's venue uuid could read that venue's name. A venue uuid is not guessable and appears on no public surface; it goes to `notify` with the rest of its wave.
- **Why `checkin` found it.** It was re-creating the function with a second parameter and wrote the revoke its own rule 2 demands for every new signature — and looked for the one on the old signature to copy. Reading the live text of a function before replacing it is the rule that paid.
- **Supersedes:** nothing. **Corrects:** `0015`'s omission.
- **Documents changed:** `STATUS.md` (the owner's statement; the finding), `03-permissions-rls.md` §8.2 (two rows), a migration (`0103`)

## DEC-153 — Certificates follow attendance through one function; re-issuing after a revocation stays carried, because a unique constraint and an idempotent early return forbid it

- **Date:** 2026-09-17 · **Decided by:** lead, as custodian of `designer` (wave 9, row L4)
- **Decision.** `0108`. (1) The certificate path had three opinions about who attended — `fan_out_certificates()` («every active check-in»), `issue_certificate()` («an active check-in exists») and `listEligibleRecipients()` (the `check_ins` of the session) — and now has one: `scoring`'s `session_attendance_complete()` (`0107`, contract 6). The fan-out is **once per member** — three days are three check-ins and one certificate. Staff cannot execute the predicate, so SCR-045's list reads it through `session_complete_attendees()`, definer, staff-only, with the `03` §1.3 org re-read. (2) **`attendance_certificate_sync(p_session, p_member)`** is contract 5's third hook (`DEC-151`): not complete → revoke every live attendance certificate of that member for that session, **whichever check-in it names**; complete, the session completed, certificates on and **no certificate row of that kind** → enqueue the issue job under `11` §2.5's key. A certificate's `check_in_id` is the member's check-in on **the last day they attended, by the day's start** — never by `created_at`, which is the transaction's start and identical for rows written together (the wave's second meeting with that trap, this time in the lead's own first draft, caught by its own test on the second run).
- ★ **Named difference 3 is narrowed.** `DEC-151` said «a member re-added after completion gets their certificate». **True when no certificate was ever issued** — a member marked present the morning after, which today yields nothing at one day too, because the fan-out fires only on the edge into `completed`. **Not true after a revocation**, and this entry says why rather than leaving it a mystery a third wave: `certificates` is `unique (org_id, session_id, member_id, kind)` and `issue_certificate()` opens with «return the existing row» (`REQ-CRT-003`, idempotency) — **a revoked row included**. Lifting it means a partial unique index `where state <> 'revoked'`, a second serial, and **two rows per member on SCR-045 and in `/app/me/certificates`**, neither of which is this wave's screen. **Wave 7's carry stays carried, with its cause known and its fix sized**; the sync function returns early on any existing row precisely so it never enqueues a job that would be a no-op that looks like work.
- **At one day all of it is what it was**: the predicate is «an active check-in on the one day», so the same set fans out, the same `no_check_in` is raised and the same names are listed. `designer-certificates`, `certificates-designs`, `checkin-removal` and `checkin-late-job-hooks` pass unmodified.
- **`scoring`'s written request** for this row was due after contract 6 was promoted; the lead did it directly once `0107` was green, as custodian, rather than wait for a message asking for what both already agreed.
- **Supersedes:** `DEC-151`'s wording of named difference 3.
- **Documents changed:** `STATUS.md` (row L4, named difference 3), `03-permissions-rls.md` §8.2 (six rows), a migration (`0108`)

## DEC-154 — Contract 11's two halves are promoted together, and its «announce once» guard is keyed on what was announced, not on having been called

- **Date:** 2026-09-17 · **Decided by:** lead, at the promotion of `0111` (`notify`) and `0112` (`sessions`)
- **Together, or not at all.** `0111` makes `sessions_notify()`'s change branch stand down while `kareem.days_writer` is set, because `session_days_changed()` then announces the whole change once; `0106`'s day-aware `schedule_session()` sets that flag and did not yet make the call. Either migration alone means a day-aware reschedule **announces nothing, moves no reminder and enqueues no calendar job**. Both teammates saw it independently — `notify` wrote it down as the order its file depends on — and they are consecutive migrations in one push. `main`'s app never sets the flag, so `main` is unaffected by either (contract 2).
- **The defect the promotion found.** `session_days_changed()` guarded against a double announcement with a transaction-local mark keyed on the **session**, set on **entry** — before the state guard. So a call that returned early, because the session was not published yet, **consumed** the mark, and the real change later in the same transaction was silenced. `sessions`' own new case — «ONE reschedule notice for a whole day-set change» — expected 1 notice and read **0** the moment the two files met. Each track's tests were green alone: `notify`'s never made an early-returning call first, and `sessions`' had no function to call. **It existed only at the seam**, which is what promoting the two together was for.
- **Decision.** The mark is keyed on the session **and the resulting day set** (`md5` of the after-snapshot), and it is **set only where a notice is actually sent**. A retry of the same change is still suppressed; a second, different change in one transaction is a second fact and is announced; an early return consumes nothing. In production each RPC is its own transaction, so **no member was ever affected** — but a guard whose failure mode is «a member is never told their room moved» is the wrong way round, and the cost of the other failure is a duplicate mail.
- **Process, stated because it bent a rule.** A function has one writer, and this one is `notify`'s. The lead changed it **inside the promotion**, before `0111` was committed, rather than leave two staged renames in a shared index while a message went round; `notify` was told the exact lines and owns the function from here. `notify` also made `session_days_changed()` read either snapshot shape (`a79f83b`) after finding `0106` snapshots whole rows with no `venue_label` — so a day that changes room is announced whichever shape arrives.
- **Two more named differences at one day, from `notify`'s record, both approved:** (4) is now **unconditional** — `notify` fed the database's own `jsonb` string through `renderEmail()` and the reminder body read «الموعد: 2026-09-19T06:37:03.319767+00:00»; a Mailpit hop cannot change a rendered body, so the capture asked for in `DEC-151` adds nothing. **(5) is new: a reminder mail names its venue.** `08` §3.2's four reminder templates print «المكان: {{venue}}» and `send_reminder_notification()` has never put a `venue` in the payload, so every reminder since M3 has read «المكان: » and nothing. At several days it cannot stay missing — the room can differ per meeting — so the payload carries the day's venue, and at one day an empty line becomes the room's name.
- **One ledger line accepted as written:** `tests/components/me/calendar-page.test.tsx` — three fixture literals name `id`, `dayPosition` and `dayCount` for the one-day session they already described; no assertion changed.
- **Documents changed:** `STATUS.md` (contract 11, named differences 4 and 5, the ledger), `03-permissions-rls.md` §8.2 (seven rows), two migrations (`0111`, `0112`)

## DEC-155 — Wave 9, sync 2: every track's SQL is promoted (`0102`–`0116`); the attendance key's trailing epoch changes what `05` §2.1 says it means; the ledger has seven lines and no changed expectation

- **Date:** 2026-09-17 · **Decided by:** lead (wave 9, sync 2)
- **Promoted, each against the existing suites unmodified:** `0102` contract 5's two functions with `main`'s text · `0103` the security revoke (`DEC-152`) · `0104`–`0105` check-in per day · `0106` `schedule_session()` on the day set · `0107` the predicate · `0108` certificates follow attendance (`DEC-153`) · `0109`–`0110` a calendar entry and a reminder stream per day · `0111`–`0112` contract 11 as a pair (`DEC-154`) · `0113`–`0114` the award at completion and the missed day · `0115`–`0116` content scope and phase by scope. Promotions were applied with `supabase migration up --local` — never a reset mid-build, which would cut a teammate's running suite — and `applyProposed()` became a no-op for a promoted file, so no teammate's test needed an `existsSync` guard. A clean `db:reset` from `0001` is a final-gate item; CI applies the whole chain on every push regardless.
- ★ **The attendance award's key, and what it does to `05` §2.1.** `scoring` built `check_in:check_in:<the check-in on the last day attended>:<member>:v<N>`, where **`N` is one more than the member's reversed attendance awards for that session**. The first award is `v1` — `main`'s key, byte for byte. A re-add after a reversal is `v2`, **with no dependence on any timestamp** — the plan's «latest created check-in» would have been arbitrary for rows written in one transaction, a trap this wave met three times (`ad43ddb`, `0108`, here). `05` §2.1 says the trailing epoch «is bumped only by a `DECISIONS.md`-logged re-award; nothing ever writes anything but `v1`». **That sentence is no longer true for the `check_in` rule, and this entry is the log it asks for**: for attendance the epoch is mechanical and counts reversals; for every other rule it stays as `05` wrote it. **At one day a re-added check-in's ledger key is now `…:v2` where `main` writes `…:v1`** — an internal identifier no screen shows and no existing test asserts, so it is recorded here rather than listed as a named difference in behaviour. The ledger row's amount, reason, source and `source_id` are `main`'s.
- **What the promotions found, beyond `DEC-152` … `DEC-154`.** (1) `content`: the «بعد الجلسة» visibility rule is copied into **five** policies — the table, its storage twin, `material_versions_read`, `material_pages_read` and the page-image bucket's — found by dumping the `exists()` body as owner and as member rather than guessing; fixing the two the plan named would have shipped a row readable whose version and page images were not (`0054`'s bug again). (2) `checkin`: a live code minted a minute before a day's ceiling is still inside `valid_until` after the next day has begun; typed in the next day's room it would have answered `session_ended` — wrong, and a disclosure `REQ-CHK-004` forbids, since only a real code could produce it. A code now names its day only while that day is taking attendance. (3) The lead's own `REQ-TSK-002` guard failed on `content`'s `rescope_task()` and **the guard was wrong**: it had «the day» on the check-in path, and a task naming its day is `DEC-121`'s design. It now forbids a task meeting **attendance**, keeps a tripwire listing every function that names a task table and a day, and was re-proven against a planted violation.
- **The untouched-suite ledger at sync 2 — seven pre-existing test files modified, no expectation changed in any.** Read line by line by the lead: `rls/realtime.test.ts` and `unit/admin-audit-labels.test.ts` (the lead's, earlier entries); `rls/db.ts` (the harness: `applyProposed()`'s no-op); `components/me/calendar-page.test.tsx` (`notify` — three fixture literals name the one day they already described); `components/browse/fixtures.tsx` (`sessions` — a shared fixture gains `days: []`); `components/checkin/remove-check-in-form.test.tsx` (`checkin` — the render call passes the one day the file was always about); `components/scoring/points-history-list.test.tsx` (`scoring` — a harness line, plus six **new** cases that belong in a new file and are being moved). `content` took the better route and made its new DTO field optional, so its five component tests are untouched against the wave's base.
- **Carried, each with its cause:** re-issuing a certificate after a revocation (`DEC-153` — a unique constraint and an idempotent early return); a proposal's own material showing its row and never its version or pages (three policies `inner join sessions`; predates `DEC-121`, found by `content`, deliberately not fixed); `session_venue_label()` open to `authenticated` with no caller check (`DEC-152`, low); a multi-day poster's date (`DEC-151`); `sessions_notify()` silent on an end-only change at one day (unchanged by contract 2).
- **Supersedes:** `05-scoring-engine.md` §2.1's sentence on the trailing epoch, for the `check_in` rule only.
- **Documents changed:** `STATUS.md` (sync 2, the ledger, contracts 3–8 and 11, named differences 3–5, carried), `05-scoring-engine.md` §2.1 (the epoch, under this entry), `03-permissions-rls.md` §8.2 (`0102`–`0116`'s rows, by the promotions)

## DEC-156 — Wave 9, sync 3: the last four migrations; the public card's row gains `day_count`, which is the wave's one deliberately changed expectation; and contract 5 is whole

- **Date:** 2026-09-17 · **Decided by:** lead (wave 9, sync 3)
- **Promoted:** `0117` (`notify` — `session_day_place()` revoked from members: it had copied the grant beside it and inherited `DEC-152`'s hazard) · `0118` (`sessions` — the public card's count) · `0119` (lead — `session_venue_label()` revoked from members, closing `DEC-152`'s low finding) · `0120` (`checkin` — contract 5's call sites). **Every `supabase/proposed/` folder is empty.**
- ★ **The public card's row gains `day_count`, and an existing test's expectation changed — once, on purpose.** `/s/[id]` is anonymous; `session_days` grants `select` to `authenticated` only, and a session that crosses midnight is indistinguishable from a two-day one by its two ends alone — so the card cannot say «3 أيام» without the count, and the count travels in `session_public_card()`'s own row rather than through a new anonymous endpoint (one integer on an existing endpoint is a smaller surface than a second endpoint). `tests/rls/sessions-public-card.test.ts` pins that row as an **allowlist** — «these keys are ALL there is», so a column can never arrive by being selected accidentally — and it failed at promotion, which is the guard doing exactly what it was written to do: **force a conscious edit**. The lead made it, with the review in the test's own comment: a number of meetings, no member, no venue beyond the one already public, nothing per day; at one day it is `1`, `main`'s app ignores the key, and the rendered card is unchanged. **It is the only line in the ledger marked «expectation changed: yes»**, and `DEC-150`'s sentence — «a changed expectation for a one-day session is a defect» — stands for every other file: this one changed because a public payload was widened deliberately, not because a one-day session behaves differently. `sessions` could not have seen it: its own run preceded `0118` being in the database. **Like contract 11's guard, it existed only at the promotion.**
- **`DEC-152`'s low finding is closed, not carried.** `notify` audited every caller of `session_venue_label()` and the lead verified it against the catalogue: seven call sites, every one inside a `SECURITY DEFINER` function, no application or worker code, no policy, no view. So the plain revoke costs nothing, and a grant nobody uses is a door rather than a feature. `tests/rls/definer-exposure.test.ts` gains the case: a member holding another org's venue uuid is refused.
- **Contract 5 is whole.** `check_in()`, `mark_checked_in_manually()` and `remove_check_in()` each end in two `perform` lines — `scoring`'s hook and the lead's — and their source names none of `points_ledger`, `award_points`, `enqueue_job`, `certificates` or `revoke_certificate`, which `checkin` asserts from `pg_get_functiondef`. The lookup of a certificate **by `check_in_id`** is retired with it: removing day 1 revokes a certificate that names day 3. 165 cases across the seventeen files that cover removal, awards and certificates, the pre-existing ones unmodified.
- **`checkInDay()` and `resolveDay()` are generic** (`sessions`' request): a `SessionDay[]` in is a `SessionDay` out, so the day's own switch is read off the element that was resolved. `checkin`'s SCR-044 stat «أكمل كل الأيام» reads the lead's existing `session_complete_attendees()` (`0108`) — staff-only, one call, the one definition — rather than a new aggregate from `scoring`.
- **Documents changed:** `STATUS.md` (sync 3, the ledger's one «yes», carried), `03-permissions-rls.md` §8.2 (nine rows), four migrations (`0117`–`0120`)

## DEC-157 — Wave 9, sync 4: what opening the captures and writing the owner's order found — `0121`, `0122`, contract 9 enforced, the attendance CSV's shape, and two refinements of the rulings

- **Date:** 2026-09-17 · **Decided by:** lead (wave 9, sync 4)
- ★ **The window that could not be taken back, closed in SQL (`0121`).** Writing row L9 meant reading `main`'s worker job by job against the new schema. Between the merge and Railway's redeploy — a window that has been hours, three merges running — `main`'s `award_presenter_points` loops over **check-in rows**, so a three-day workshop would pay its presenter three `attendee_bonus` rows per attendee, partial attendees included, onto a ledger nothing can delete from (invariant 9). Every other old-worker behaviour at more than one day is late, transient or harmless, and is tabulated in `STATUS`. **Decision:** the rule moves into `award_points()` — an `attendee_bonus` is written only for the attendee's epoch check-in and only when that attendee completed the session — so SQL is the authority whichever worker calls. `scoring` built it as `0113`'s body with one branch added, its cases written **as the old worker's loop**; inert at one day, `award-presenter-points` and `award-points` unmodified. **And the owner's order says: nobody schedules a session of more than one day until the worker is on the merge commit**, with a scoped, idempotent repair if that rule is ever broken.
- ★ **Contract 9 is enforced, not remembered.** `PhaseInput.days` is optional on purpose — no one-day caller and no existing test had to change — and the cost is that an omission is silent: given the stored window alone, `sessionPhase()` answers `live` from day 1's start to day 3's end. Opening the public card's capture found it saying «جارية الآن» between two days while the event page said «التسجيل مفتوح» for the same session at the same instant; reading every call site found **four** day-less readers (the public card, the event DTO and the `relation` derived from it, the profile's session list, the RSVP panel). All four are fixed by their owners. **Decision:** `days` stays optional, and `tests/unit/session-phase-reads-days.test.ts` reads every `sessionPhase(` call site in `src/` and fails one that does not show where its days come from — named in the argument, declared with them, typed `PhaseInput`, or a written `phase-days:` reason. Its list of open sites could only shrink and is empty.
- ★ **The public card's row gains `days` (`0122`) — the second deliberately changed expectation of the wave, and the last.** Two instants per day, ordered; **no id, no position, no venue**, asserted key by key in `sessions-public-card.test.ts` by a lead-reviewed edit. A boolean «a day is running» would disclose less and would put `betweenDays()` in SQL beside the TypeScript one — and two implementations of one rule is how the defect happened. `session_days` gains no `anon` grant.
- **The attendance CSV (row L5) is long, not wide.** At one day the per-session file is wave 7's byte for byte — six headers, one line per member, no «اليوم» column with one value in it. From two days it is one line per member **per day**, the day in contract 7's words through `dayLabel()` over the Arabic source, and «أكمل الحضور» last — `session_attendance_complete()`'s answer, which is who gets the points and the certificate. The column count does not depend on the day count. The org-wide export is already one line per check-in and is unchanged.
- **Ruling 3, refined: the add control in a group's header OPENS that group's form.** `content`'s first build mounted an open add form under every group — eight open forms on a three-day workshop, a 9,059 px page for a presenter on a phone, with the header control reduced to an anchor. In the grouped layout the form sits behind its header control, closed on load; the flat one-day layout is untouched.
- **Ruling 4, its wording half: the phase chip is relative to the scope too.** `0116` made «بعد» mean «after that day» for a day-scoped material, and the chip still said «بعد الجلسة» on slides a member could already open with two days to run. A material that names a day reads «قبل اليوم» / «بعد اليوم»; a session-scoped one reads exactly what it read. Driven by the item's scope, never by the day count.
- **A lead's step added to the handoff: the data-shaped rehearsal.** The owner's rehearsal runs against a **schema-only** dump, which cannot show what a backfill does to rows. Before the PR is marked ready the lead builds a bare Postgres at the last pushed migration, **commits** `main`'s own RLS fixture plus the shapes it lacks, applies the wave's files, and compares every pre-existing column of every row. This wave: 107 rows and a 30-job queue identical except `calendar_events.updated_at`, which `0101`'s backfill moves and nothing reads.
- **Found and carried, not changed:** `rotate_codes` is registered in the worker and has **no crontab entry** — it has never run in production, and codes are minted on demand by the host view's `ensure_check_in_code()`. Named difference 1 is therefore a property of the task, not of production today. Whether to schedule it or delete it is not this wave's subject.
- **The untouched-suite ledger:** one more «expectation changed: yes» — `rls/sessions-public-card.test.ts`, the same file as `DEC-156`'s, for `days`. Every other line stands as recorded.
- **Documents changed:** `STATUS.md` (sync 4, row L5, row L9 and the owner's order, the ledger, carried), `03-permissions-rls.md` §8.2 (`0121`'s four rows, `0122`'s two), two migrations (`0121`, `0122`)

## DEC-158 — A correction to `DEC-157`: `rotate_codes` is not unscheduled

- **Date:** 2026-09-17 · **Decided by:** lead, an hour after writing the claim
- **What `DEC-157` said, and it was wrong:** «`rotate_codes` is registered in the worker and has no crontab entry — it has never run in production.» The lead read the crontab and stopped reading. `start_session` — which **is** in the crontab, every minute — enqueues `rotate_codes` once for every session it moves to `in_progress`, under the key `code:<session>:first`. So the task runs **once per started session**; it has no *periodic* schedule, and every later code is minted on demand by the host view's `ensure_check_in_code()`, which is how a multi-day session's second and third days get theirs.
- **What follows.** Named difference 1 (`DEC-151`) **does** describe production, at that one run. Nothing is carried: there is no missing schedule to add and no dead task to delete. `DEC-157`'s other paragraphs stand.
- **Why an entry and not an edit:** this log is append-only (rule 3 of the handoff protocol), and a wrong sentence with its correction beneath it is what that rule is for.
- **Documents changed:** `STATUS.md` (sync 4's table and *Carried* — the row removed)

## DEC-159 — Wave 9, sync 5: what the demonstrable found that no suite could, a nit withdrawn, and the wave closes

- **Date:** 2026-09-17 · **Decided by:** lead (wave 9, the freeze)
- ★ **The demonstrable runs from an EMPTY session on a production build with the real worker, and that is why it found three defects every suite had passed.** (1) `content`'s shared re-scope chip received an **inline closure from a Server Component** — «Event handlers cannot be passed to Client Component props» — so the event page of any multi-day session holding content fell into its error boundary **for a manager, in a real build only**; jsdom renders everything client-side and cannot produce it. Fixed by binding the `"use server"` export (`8b8e995`). (2) A **brand-new workshop could not take a day's material**: the slot's empty state returned before the grouped branch, so there was no group header to press and ruling 3's «pressing the control is the choice» did not exist until something had been added the other way. Every fixture seeded content; none met the empty state (`a11d071`). (3) On the schedule form an **added day's start read «لم يُحدَّد بعد»** above its own end time — a datetime string handed to a date-mode picker (`4e0b075`). **Decision, for every later wave:** a feature's demonstrable starts from nothing, as a person does, on a production build, and keeps the server's own words (`STUBBED_SERVER_LOG`).
- **A lead's nit, withdrawn.** At sync 4 the lead asked `sessions` to stop a wrapped line beginning with «·» on the event page. `sessions` applied the same change to the public card, where **wave 7 had decided the opposite on purpose** (`58ab535`: «· حتى 8:27 م» is one unbreakable clause) **and pinned it with two assertions** — which the untouched e2e suite then failed on both projects. Restored byte for byte (`d72ed4a`). The ledger did its job against the lead.
- **Every toast is announced in Arabic.** Radix names the toast region «Notifications (F8)» and prefixes each announcement with «Notification»; since M9 an Arabic toast reached a screen reader as «Notification تتم معالجة الصورة الآن…». The shell now passes «إشعار» to both. Found by accident — a strict-mode locator matched the live region (`07e16a0`). Invariant 10's reach includes what is never seen.
- **The spec's clock, stated because it looks like a product defect and is not:** shifting `session_days` to move time, without ageing the check-ins already recorded, makes a member's own yesterday overlap their today (`REQ-CHK-013`'s exclusion compares stored windows). Time passing moves both; the demonstrable's clock moves both.
- **Carried out of the freeze, each small and each with an owner:** the «مطلوب» marker on the manual-mark form's three controls, dropped when they moved onto `ui/field` because the marker joins the accessible name and the form's labels are asserted verbatim (lead, M13); `DayWindow.id`/`position` could be optional for the public card's id-less windows (lead, contained in one mapping); the attendance table scrolls sideways inside its container at 390 px from two days up, as the one-day table's last column already did (`console`, M13).
- **The untouched-suite ledger closes at eight files and one changed expectation** (`DEC-156`, `DEC-157`). **No existing e2e spec is modified.**
- **Documents changed:** `STATUS.md` (sync 5, the final gates, the contracts held, the rows closed), `docs/plan/notes/wave-10-lead.md` (new)

## DEC-160 — Wave 10 is the survey and the email studio, with three carried fixes; `event` builds the survey whole, on opus; a stored survey response names no member; and the mail renderer moves into a package only after its output is pinned

- **Date:** 2026-09-17 · **Decided by:** owner (the wave-10 brief, `docs/plan/notes/wave-10-lead.md`: the two features, the three carried items, what is not this wave), the staffing, the file-level map, the contracts and the two foundations by the lead
- **Supersedes:** `DEC-150`'s wave-9 map as the map in force (kept in `CLAUDE.md` as the record); `DEC-137`'s and `DEC-150`'s placement of `app/sessions/[id]/rate/**`, `components/event/{ratings,star-rating}.tsx`, `lib/dal/ratings.ts` and `messages/*/ratings.json` with `sessions` (they return to `event`, which is spawned); `DEC-147`'s placement of `app/admin/emails/**` with `console` (it returns to `notify`, as `DEC-085` said it would); `DEC-137`'s placement of `app/me/certificates/**` with `content` (it returns to `designer` for the re-issue); `DEC-153`'s custody of the four `0108` functions with the lead (they are `designer`'s, which is spawned). **Narrows** `DEC-074` and `DEC-094` (the survey's storage — §3 below) and **corrects** `DEC-081` on a point of fact (§4).

### 1 · Both post-merge confirmations were read, not asked

The Railway worker is **RUNNING on `f2ead54`** — PR #26's merge commit, deployed 2026-09-17 10:47 UTC (`railway status`, a read). The `DEC-152` statement is recorded as run in `STATUS.md` (the owner's production reads: `f / f / f`). `main`'s CI is green on the merge commit. Nobody was asked.

### 2 · Who builds the survey — decided before the map, as the brief required

**`event`, end to end, on opus.** `16` §16.4 wrote the survey against `event` with a file list that is still exactly right; what went stale is `.claude/agents/event.md`, which is regenerated with the other nine anyway. The alternatives were weighed against the code, not the names:

- **Split it — `sessions` the member side, `console` the admin side.** It follows today's ownership (the rate screen has been `sessions'` since wave 7, `app/admin/**` is `console`'s) and it is wrong for this feature: the survey's one hard requirement is a storage guarantee (`REQ-SUR-009`) that spans the member's write, the worker's write and the staff's read. A seam through the middle of it is a seam through the invariant — the submit RPC on one side, the results function on the other, and the rule «nothing links them» owned by neither.
- **Give it whole to `sessions`.** Possible, and it would cost a track whose note is three thousand lines about forms, timelines and schedules a wave it has no other work in. `event`'s note is 253 lines and §0 and §4 of it are the rating-anonymity record the survey has to be read against.
- **Opus, not the sonnet on file**, for `DEC-137`'s and `DEC-150`'s reason: the track writes definer functions on an invariant that **cannot be repaired afterwards** — `16` §9.2a: «once written correlated, always correlated; a fix next quarter does not protect the people who answered this quarter».

**Spawned:** `event` (opus ★), `notify` (opus), `designer` (opus), `content` (sonnet). **Not spawned, held by the lead as custodian:** `sessions`, `checkin`, `scoring`, `console`, `platform`, `branding` — including `sessions'` eight and `console`'s six `ui/` primitives. The survey's two touches on `console`'s files (a rail entry, the audited export's registration) are custodian rows on `event`'s written request.

### 3 · The survey's storage contract — the lead's, published before any table exists

`DEC-094` decorrelated two writes **in time**. Read against the code, time is not the only join, and the design below removes the thing being joined rather than blurring it. **What the code says today:** a rating is a plain RLS `insert` (no RPC) with `submitted_at timestamptz default now()`, never coarsened; `edited_at` is written from JavaScript at millisecond precision; the presenter's comment list is `array_agg(comment order by submitted_at)`; and `ratings_award_points` leaves a member-attributed `points_ledger` row with a precise `created_at` seconds after every rating. Any survey row that carries a member and an instant can be joined to all of that.

1. ★ **A stored survey response names no member.** `survey_responses` and `survey_answers` carry **no `member_id`, no `check_in_id`, no `rating_id` and no timestamp column of any kind**, and no foreign-key path leads from a response to a member. «One member, one response» (`REQ-SUR-003`) lives in a separate **`survey_participations (survey_id, member_id)`** — also without a timestamp — written by the member's own action; a second submission is refused from it by name. `DEC-074`'s «`survey_responses` — one per member per survey» becomes «one per participation, **unlinkably**». This is a secret ballot: the register says who voted, the box says what was voted, and nothing says which.
2. **Two writes, still decorrelated, still through the queue.** The action validates, writes the rating exactly as today, records the participation, and enqueues the response through `public.enqueue_job()` with a **jittered `run_at`**. The payload is the survey id and the answers — **no member, no rating, no check-in, no request id** — and the job key is **null or random, never derived from the member** (`survey:<survey>:<member>` would be the leak in one string). The jitter is no longer what hides the rater; it is what keeps transaction ids, heap order and WAL position from pairing a response with the participation written beside the rating.
3. **No client role can select a response, an answer, or another member's participation.** Results leave the database through **one definer function** that applies the minimum-count withhold to **every** question type (`REQ-SUR-006`); the results screen and the CSV both call it, so «the withhold applies to the export exactly as to the screen» (`REQ-SUR-007`) is true by construction, and `xmin` and `ctid` are never readable. `REQ-SUR-005`'s explicit presenter case stays: refused, by the function and by the absence of any policy.
4. **`ratings` holds no instant finer than a day.** `submitted_at` **and `edited_at`** are coarsened by a `before insert or update` trigger — which covers `main`'s app, which writes both — with a backfill of existing rows in the same migration; `session_rating_aggregates.comments` stops ordering by `submitted_at` (submission order is itself a disclosure to a presenter who watched people leave). The carried `ratings.edited_at` finding (waves 6–7) closes here.
5. **The submit writes no audit row, and no log line, breadcrumb or job payload carries a member beside an answer.** The worker task logs a count, never a payload.
6. **The residue, stated rather than hidden:** while a response waits in the queue, its job row carries the answers and a precise `created_at` inside `graphile_worker`, reachable by `service_role` alone and deleted on completion; and in a survey one person answered, the participation table says who — which is what the withhold is for, at read time. Neither is closed by more machinery; both are in `12`.

**What this costs, on purpose:** a member cannot re-open or edit their answers, and the PDPL self-export (`REQ-PRF-006`) contains «you answered this survey» and not the answers — an answer that cannot be attributed is not that member's personal data. **`REQ-SUR-009`'s acceptance test is restated for it**: the ±N-minute set is vacuous when a response has no instant, so the RLS suite asserts the structure instead — no member, check-in, rating or timestamp column on the two tables, no foreign-key path from a response to a member, a payload with no member in it, and a `ratings` row whose two instants are midnight.

**Tables are the lead's** (wave 9's rule, kept): `event` names every column in its plan, the lead lands the DDL at sync 1 with the `02` entities `DEC-074` said it wrote and never did — **`02`, `03` §8.2, `11` and `12` contain no trace of the survey today**; they are written with the tables, under this entry.

### 4 · The email studio — two facts that change its first week

- ★ **There are no mail goldens.** `DEC-081` and `REQ-NTF-009` promise that «the existing golden tests do not move». No such tests exist: `tests/unit/mail-*.test.ts` pin fragments by `toBe()` and diff the template keys against the matrix, and nothing pins one whole rendered message. **So `notify`'s first code task is to pin today's output** — subject, text and HTML for **all 25 keys** over fixed sample payloads, generated from the renderer **as it stands on `main`**, committed before a line of it changes. «Byte-identical for an org that has not touched its templates» is the wave's one-day rule, and like wave 9's it has to be provable before the feature exists.
- **One renderer means one package.** `REQ-NTF-010`: «there is exactly one mail renderer; the preview is not a second implementation». The worker is a workspace the Next build cannot import — `worker/dist` is gitignored, its imports are `NodeNext` with `.js` suffixes, and `render.ts` states the boundary as a rule. The repo's own answer is `@kareem/designer-runtime` (`DEC-017`, `DEC-029`). **`packages/mail-runtime` (`@kareem/mail-runtime`)**: isomorphic, no `node:` import, built first by the root `build`, copied by the worker image. **The lead scaffolds it and moves `render.ts` and `templates.ts` mechanically, after the goldens are committed and with the goldens as the proof**; `notify` owns `packages/mail-runtime/src/**` from there and builds the block compiler in it. `package.json`, the lock (`npm run lockfile`), `worker/Dockerfile` and the build order stay the lead's.
- **Counted, not quoted:** the matrix in force (`0062`) has 39 rows, **25 with an email channel**; `DEFAULT_TEMPLATES` has **25** keys; `08` §3.2's table lists **23**. `DEC-081`'s «22 against 25» is one behind on one side. `notify` writes the reconciliation; the lead edits `08`.
- **Ruled at sync 1, named now so the plan answers them:** where the platform library lives (`notification_templates.org_id` is `not null` — there is no platform-owned row today, and an eighth exception to invariant 5 needs a reason the code constants do not already give); what a block template's row offers `main`'s worker in the merge → Railway window (its `body` is `not null` — the generated text alternative is the obvious value); how `/api/webhooks/resend` reaches `update_email_delivery_by_provider()`, which is `service_role`-only, when `service_role` is never on Vercel (invariant 7); and what an org's existing string override becomes in the editor.

### 5 · `ui/reorderable-list` is the lead's, on day one

`REQ-SUR-002` and `REQ-NTF-009` are both specified against «the shared `ui/reorderable-list`» (`16` §10.2.1: «three lists, one primitive … buttons first, drag layered on»). It does not exist; the only reordering in the product is the studio's layer list, typed on `DesignDocument`. Two tracks need it in their first story, so it is built while they plan: ▲▼ on every row, named by the row they move (`aria-describedby`), taps alone (`SC 2.5.7`), a live announcement of the new position — and **no drag this wave**; drag is the enhancement and nobody needs it to conform.

### 6 · The three carried items, as sized by reading the code

- **Certificates, re-issued (`designer`).** `unique (org_id, session_id, member_id, kind)` becomes a partial unique index over rows that are not revoked (the lead's DDL); `issue_certificate()`'s early return and `attendance_certificate_sync()`'s «any row» gain the same predicate; the second certificate takes the **next serial** — `allocate_serial()` stays gapless (`DEC-010`) and the revoked one keeps verifying as revoked. SCR-045 already renders two rows for one member sanely (three tables by state, keyed by id); `/app/me/certificates` shows two cards; `getCertificateDesign()`'s `mine[0]` would name the **revoked** row's design under «صدرت بـ» and is the one reader that assumes one row.
- **A multi-day poster's date (`designer`).** The date is one binding — `session.startsAt`, formatted in the runtime — and `poster_render_context()` selects `starts_at` alone. A range needs a new binding and a **new seed migration** (`DEC-149` §3); `tests/unit/designer-library.test.ts` names its two seed files literally and must learn a third. **No parity golden moves** — the 28 cases are synthetic documents with literal text — and a one-day poster must render the same characters it renders today.
- **A proposal's own material (`content`).** Three policies `inner join sessions`, so no branch is reached for a row whose `session_id` is null — **staff included**. No page exists for such a material (conversion waits for carry-over, by design), so the visible half of the defect is narrower than its description: **an admin reviewing a proposal cannot open the file the proposer attached** (`REQ-PRO-004`: «visible to admins»), because the download reads `material_versions` under RLS and gets nothing. The fix is the three predicates and the link.

### 7 · What carries over from wave 9 unchanged

Additive migrations, because the owner pushes before merging and `main`'s app and worker run on the new schema first; the old signature dropped in the same file as the new one; tables the lead's, behaviour the tracks', a function one writer; **the untouched-suite ledger** — an existing test changes only with a line saying why, and here the rule has two subjects: a session with no survey, and an org that has not touched its templates. ★ **The owner's migration order is drafted at sync 1, not at the freeze** (lesson 1 of the brief): what `main`'s worker does with a block template, with a coarsened rating and with a second certificate is read before the SQL is promoted, not after.

- **Two routes are added to `04` §4** (`DEC-083`'s rule — no route is built before its entry exists): `/app/admin/surveys` and `/app/admin/surveys/[templateId]` — the survey templates an org reuses (`REQ-SUR-001`), **SCR-065**. Attaching a template to a session happens on SCR-064, so the schedule form is not touched. Any route the email studio needs beyond `/app/admin/emails` is named in `notify`'s plan and lands with sync 1's entry.
- **`01` is corrected for `DEC-124` in four places**: `REQ-SUR-002` («مقياس 1–5»), `REQ-RAT-006`'s quoted copy, and the two survey requirements that still speak of «the org's numeral setting», which `DEC-124` abolished.
- **Documents changed:** `CLAUDE.md` (the wave-10 map; wave 9 demoted to the record), all ten `.claude/agents/*.md`, `STATUS.md` (the wave-10 block), `01-prd.md` (`REQ-SUR-002`, `003`, `004`, `007`, `008`, `009`, `REQ-RAT-006` — numerals and §3's storage contract), `04-architecture.md` §4 and `09-sitemap-screens.md` (SCR-065, the two routes)
